claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

1. **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you wanting to claim Child Benefit for?** Please provide their names and ages.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Let me gather some more information about your situation.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after him (for example on food, clothes or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex does live with me, but actually he's been in local authority care for a couple of months now. He doesn't come home to stay with me though - he's there full-time at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**How long has Alex been in local authority care? Has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been more than 8 weeks. It's been about 12 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

**Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you? For example, does he spend at least 24 hours a week at home, or does he come home for at least 2 nights in a row each week, or for 7 days or more in a row?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't come home regularly like that. He's at the care home full-time, so he's not spending 24 hours a week with me or coming home for nights like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I have one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex - for example on clothes, presents, food, pocket money, or other things for his upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not able to spend money on him regularly at the moment.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While you live in the UK and Alex is 8 years old (under 16), the key issue is that Alex has been in local authority care for approximately 12 weeks. According to Child Benefit rules, you usually stop being entitled to Child Benefit after a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks.

There are exceptions to this rule that would allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit, such as:
- If Alex spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you
- If he spends at least 2 consecutive nights each week at home, or 7 or more consecutive days at home
- If you're regularly spending money on him

However, you've confirmed that Alex doesn't come home regularly and you're not currently able to spend money on him regularly. Since none of these exceptions apply to your situation, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if Alex starts spending regular time at home or you begin contributing financially to his upkeep - you may want to contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility again.
